consensus_summary: Name primarily symbolizes the essential character, identity, authority, presence, power, and reputation of the person (supremely God or Jesus), so that to know, call on, hallow, or act in the name is to engage the person himself; alternatives treat complementary facets such as delegated agency, temple presence, renown, dominion in naming, new identity, or ownership.
book_summary: Name is the covenant identity of a house, consisting of the three things appointed by its Head and kept in the ark: the Word (manna), the covenant law (stone tables), and the fruitful priesthood (Aaron’s budded rod); a counterfeit substitutes any of these, the Name is taken in vain by rejecting/replacing any of them, and a bride takes her Husband’s Name by entering His house under His authority.
book_core_identification: covenant identity of a house as the triad of Word + law + priesthood (ark contents)
boundary_disagreement: None; the book’s specific triadic ark-contents identification is simply absent from the consensus and its listed alternatives rather than a boundary adjustment of the same referent.
material_contradiction: None; the book’s primary identification does not negate the consensus character/authority sense but replaces it with an unmentioned symbolic referent.
rationale: Minimum cores differ in kind: consensus (and every alternative) centers on the person’s revealed nature/authority, while the book centers on a concrete tripartite covenant furniture set that constitutes house identity. No consensus response or alternative even alludes to manna + tables + rod as the Name, so the identification is novel rather than a narrowing, broadening, or contradiction of a shared core.
strongest_objection: The well-attested scholarly and confessional consensus equates Name with personal character/authority; the ark-contents equation is an idiosyncratic typology unsupported as the primary sense by the cited texts or standard lexicons.
